h1: The 7 Best Electric Food Choppers Under $100, From Mini Choppers to Full Processors, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Electric Food Chopper Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 electric food choppers and mini processors under $100, scored on bowl size, blade design, cordless use and ease of cleaning.
summary: The Hamilton Beach 10 Cup Food Processor is the best electric chopper under $100 if you want slicing, shredding and puree as well as chopping. The Hamilton Beach 12 Cup Stack & Snap is the bigger-batch pick, the Ninja Express Chop 200W is the best true mini chopper, and the KitchenAid 3.5 and 5 cup choppers are the stylish compact options.
intro: A $100 ceiling blurs a line that matters in the kitchen: the difference between a food chopper and a food processor. A chopper has one blade in a small bowl and does a few jobs well. A processor adds discs for slicing and shredding and a much larger bowl. Buying a processor when you wanted a chopper wastes cupboard space, and the reverse leaves you hand-slicing cabbage.

The seven machines here span both camps. Each is scored on bowl capacity, blade and disc options, power where listed, ease of cleaning and who it suits. Prices are given in brackets only, and two KitchenAid listings did not confirm a price tier, so we leave that out.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 10 Cup Food Processor
products.verdict: A 10-cup processor that slices, shreds, minces and purees, with a bowl scraper for easy cleanup.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach 10 Cup handles slicing, shredding, mincing and puree, and it has a bowl scraper and a stainless steel finish. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It wins because it covers the full job list of a kitchen processor at a price where most rivals only offer a mini chopper. Ten cups is enough for a family meal's worth of vegetables, and the bowl scraper cuts out the habit of stopping to push food down. The cost is cupboard space: a 10-cup base and bowl is not a drawer item. For a single clove of garlic or a spoonful of herbs, the work bowl is far too big.

Buy it if you want one machine for everything from coleslaw to hummus. Skip it if you have little storage.
products.idealFor: Families that prep vegetables in bulk.
products.skipIf: You only mince garlic and herbs.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 12 Cup Stack & Snap Food Processor
products.verdict: A 12-cup Stack & Snap design that avoids the twist-lock fiddle of older processors.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach 12 Cup uses a Stack & Snap assembly: the bowl, lid and chute fit together without a bayonet twist. It is sold as a vegetable chopper and processor, in the $50 to $100 bracket.

The design target is simplicity. Many processors fail on the first use because the bowl, lid and safety lock do not line up, and a snap-together approach removes that frustration. Two extra cups of capacity make it better for meal prep and batch cooking. It ranks just below the 10-cup because the listing names fewer functions, so you rely on the Hamilton Beach reputation for the rest.

Buy it if you cook large batches. Skip it if cupboard space is tight.

products.name: Ninja Food Chopper Express Chop 200W
products.verdict: A 200W mini chopper with a 16-ounce bowl for mincing, chopping, grinding and blending.
products.description:
The Ninja Express Chop is a 200W chopper with a 16-ounce bowl, aimed at mincing, chopping, grinding and blending. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket.

Sixteen ounces is two cups, the right size for an onion, a handful of herbs or a batch of salsa. The 200W motor is enough for soft vegetables and nuts, though dense carrots need a pre-cut. The reason it ranks third, not first, is scope: it does not slice or shred. As a quick chopper it is among the easiest to store and clean.

Buy it if you chop small amounts daily. Skip it if you want discs for slicing.
products.idealFor: Daily mincing of onions and herbs.

products.name: KitchenAid 5 Cup Food Chopper KFC0516ER
products.verdict: A 5-cup KitchenAid chopper in Empire red, sized between a mini and a processor.
products.description:
The KFC0516ER is a 5-cup food chopper in Empire red. It is the larger of KitchenAid's two compact choppers here.

Five cups gives room for a pot's worth of salsa or a batch of pesto, which a 16-ounce mini cannot do. It ranks fourth because the listing offers no motor wattage or blade details, so you are buying on capacity and brand. KitchenAid's colours also make it a countertop appliance you will not mind leaving out.

Buy it if you want a mid-size chopper that looks good on the counter. Skip it if you need published motor details.
pros: Five cups for sauces and dips
products.idealFor: Dips, salsas and pesto for a household.

products.name: Hamilton Beach Powerful Cordless Mini Food Processor
products.verdict: A cordless mini vegetable chopper that works anywhere without a socket.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach Cordless Mini is a battery-powered vegetable chopper, in the $50 to $100 bracket. It cuts the cord, so you can use it at a camp table or across the kitchen.

Cordless choppers appeal because they sit anywhere and tuck into a drawer. The compromise is run time and power, and the listing gives neither the capacity nor the battery life. It ranks fifth because the price puts it next to full processors, and its limited information makes that tough to justify.

Buy it if outlets are scarce or you cook outdoors. Skip it if you chop large quantities.
cons: Capacity and battery life not listed
Costs as much as full processors

products.name: KitchenAid 3.5 Cup Food Chopper KFC3516CU
products.verdict: A 3.5-cup KitchenAid chopper in Contour silver for small kitchens.
products.description:
The KFC3516CU is a 3.5-cup food chopper in Contour silver. It is the smaller KitchenAid here.

It ranks sixth because 3.5 cups sits uncomfortably between the 16-ounce Ninja and the 5-cup KitchenAid, and the listing gives no motor or blade information. For a one or two person household, though, 3.5 cups handles most daily chopping, and the silver finish suits stainless kitchens.

Buy it if you want a KitchenAid and a modest footprint. Skip it if you cook for four or more.

products.name: Cuisinart Mini Food Processor
products.verdict: A 3-cup mini processor with a reversible blade, in the $25 to $50 bracket.
products.description:
The Cuisinart Mini is a compact 3-cup processor with a reversible blade, priced in the $25 to $50 bracket.

A reversible blade has a sharp side for chopping and a dull side for grinding or mixing, which is a practical touch in such a small machine. It ranks last because 3 cups is the smallest bowl here after the Ninja, and the listing lacks power detail. Cuisinart is a respected processor name.

Buy it if you want a small, trusted-brand chopper. Skip it if you want the biggest bowl.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that value a known brand.

whatMatters.detail: A chopper has a single blade for mincing and rough chopping. A processor adds discs for slicing and shredding. Pick based on whether you cut vegetables into slices or just mince aromatics.

Sixteen ounces is two cups, enough for an onion, while 10 to 12 cups handle a family meal. Choose a bowl about twice the size of your usual batch. Too big wastes space, and too small means repeat runs.
A 200W motor chops soft vegetables and nuts but struggles with dense carrots unless pre-cut. Many listings omit wattage. Treat missing figures as a reason to lean on the brand.
Stack and snap designs and bowl scrapers cut the time spent fiddling. Dishwasher-safe parts matter for daily use. Check which pieces are top-rack safe.
A cordless chopper is flexible but limited by battery life. A corded model delivers steady power. For heavy chopping, corded is the safer choice.

faq.q: Can a chopper replace a food processor?
faq.a: For mincing and rough chopping, yes. It cannot slice or shred like a processor with discs. Match the tool to your recipes.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying one?
faq.a: Buying too small a bowl. Repeated runs waste time. Pick a bowl about twice your normal batch.

faq.q: Is the Hamilton Beach 10 cup worth it over the Ninja?
faq.a: If you slice, shred or puree, yes. The Ninja is better for daily mincing with less cleanup.

faq.q: How do I keep blades sharp?
faq.a: Avoid chopping ice, bones or hard frozen items, and hand wash the blade carefully. Dull blades bruise herbs instead of cutting them.
Many bowls and lids are top-rack safe, but blades often prefer hand washing. Check the manual for each model.

faq.q: Is a cordless chopper powerful enough?
faq.a: For soft produce, yes. It will run for a limited time on a charge. Heavy chopping suits a corded machine.

finalTake: The Hamilton Beach 10 Cup Food Processor is the best electric chopper under $100 for anyone who slices, shreds and chops, with a bowl scraper that simplifies cleanup. The 12 Cup suits batch cooks, and the Ninja Express Chop 200W is the best true mini. KitchenAid's 5 and 3.5 cup choppers are the stylish compact options. Match the bowl size to your usual batch before you buy.
